titleBlock.headline: DO-HEALTH Trial: Omega-3, Vitamin D & Exercise Additively Slow Human Epigenetic Aging
titleBlock.authors: Bischoff-Ferrari, H.A., Gängler, S., Wieczorek, M., Belsky, D.W., Ryan, J., Kressig, R.W., Stähelin, H.B., Theiler, R., Dawson-Hughes, B., Rizzoli, R., Vellas, B., Rouch, L., Guyonnet, S., Egli, A., Orav, E.J., Willett, W. & Horvath, S.
titleBlock.summary: In a 3-year multicenter 2×2×2 factorial randomized controlled trial of 777 generally healthy older adults (aged ≥70 years) from the DO-HEALTH cohort, marine algae omega-3 supplementation (1 g/day: 330 mg EPA + 660 mg DHA) alone significantly slowed three next-generation DNA methylation clocks (PC-PhenoAge, GrimAge2, and DunedinPACE), while combining omega-3 with vitamin D3 (2,000 IU/day) and strength-based home exercise (3×30 min/week) additively slowed PC-PhenoAge by 2.9 to 3.8 months over 3 years.

studyOverview.title: The Question
studyOverview.content: Can safe, scalable, low-cost public health interventions—marine omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin D3, and regular home strength exercise—slow biological aging at the molecular level in older adults aged 70+, and do their distinct mechanisms combine additively?

studyOverview.title: What They Did
studyOverview.content: Conducted a pre-specified 3-year longitudinal epigenetic bio-age analysis in n = 777 Swiss participants (mean age 75.0 yr, 59% women, 53% Nurse's Health Study healthy agers) from the 2,157-person European DO-HEALTH 2×2×2 factorial RCT across 8 randomized arms: Omega-3 (1 g/day algae oil: 330 mg EPA + 660 mg DHA), Vitamin D3 (2,000 IU/day), and SHEP Home Exercise (3×30 min/week strength vs. joint flexibility control), profiling blood Illumina EPIC (>850k CpG) DNA methylation at baseline and 36 months.

studyOverview.title: What They Found
studyOverview.content: Omega-3 alone slowed 3 of 4 primary biological clocks (PC-PhenoAge d = -0.16, GrimAge2 d = -0.32, DunedinPACE d = -0.17) and lowered 3 GrimAge plasma protein surrogates (PAI-1, Leptin, TIMP-1). Combining Omega-3 + Vitamin D3 + Exercise produced significant additive slowing on PC-PhenoAge (d = -0.24 to -0.32, equal to -2.9 to -3.8 months over 3 years), translating into clinical reductions in infections (-13%), falls (-10%), pre-frailty (-39%), and invasive cancer (-61%) in the full trial.

interventions.label: Omega-3 Alone
interventions.dose: 1,000 mg/day Marine Algae Oil (330 mg EPA + 660 mg DHA)
interventions.summary: Significantly slowed 3 of 4 primary next-generation epigenetic clocks (PC-PhenoAge, GrimAge2, DunedinPACE) and reduced 3 pro-inflammatory/metabolic GrimAge plasma protein surrogates (PAI-1, Leptin, TIMP-1). Effects were most pronounced in individuals with lower baseline blood EPA+DHA (<100 ng/mL).

interventions.label: Omega-3 + Vitamin D3
interventions.summary: Combining marine omega-3 with 2,000 IU/day vitamin D3 amplified the slowing of PC-PhenoAge (d = -0.27) and DunedinPACE (d = -0.20) while additively suppressing DNAm PAI-1, TIMP-1, and Beta-2 Microglobulin (B2M).

interventions.label: Omega-3 + Exercise
interventions.summary: Pairing omega-3 supplementation with structured home strength training (SHEP) significantly slowed PC-PhenoAge (d = -0.26) and PC-GrimAge (d = -0.18) while reducing PAI-1, TIMP-1, and B2M surrogates.

interventions.label: Triple Combination (All 3)
interventions.dose: Omega-3 (1 g/d) + Vitamin D3 (2,000 IU/d) + Exercise (3×30 min/wk)
interventions.summary: The full triple combination achieved the largest biological age deceleration on PC-PhenoAge (d = -0.24 in factorial model; d = -0.32 in direct treatment-arm comparison vs. triple placebo, equivalent to -2.9 to -3.8 months over 3 years), preserved epigenetic telomere length (PC-DNAmTL d = +0.33), and suppressed 4 GrimAge plasma protein surrogates including GDF-15 and B2M.

clinicalOutcomes.detail: Hazard Ratio 0.39 over 3 years in the full DO-HEALTH cohort (N = 2,157) when all three interventions were combined.
Odds Ratio 0.61 for progression from robust status to Fried pre-frailty across the 3-year follow-up.
Incidence Rate Ratio 0.87 for total verified infections (particularly upper respiratory and urinary tract infections).
Incidence Rate Ratio 0.90 for total falls in community-dwelling adults aged 70+.

keyFindings.title: 2nd/3rd-Gen Clocks Outperform 1st-Gen Chronological Clocks
keyFindings.desc: While 1st-generation chronological clocks (Horvath 2013, Hannum 2013) were insensitive to 3-year interventions, mortality- and pace-trained clocks (PC-PhenoAge, GrimAge2, DunedinPACE) detected consistent biological age slowing.

keyFindings.title: Baseline Omega-3 Deficiency Amplifies Epigenetic Response
keyFindings.desc: Subgroup stratification revealed that participants with lower baseline circulating EPA+DHA (<100 ng/mL) experienced significantly greater slowing of DunedinPACE and GrimAge2 upon 1 g/day algae omega-3 supplementation.

keyFindings.title: Suppression of Senescence & Fibrosis Surrogates (PAI-1, TIMP-1, GDF-15)
keyFindings.desc: Deconstructing GrimAge into its constituent plasma protein surrogates showed that omega-3 and the triple combination specifically lowered DNAm PAI-1 (a core SASP/thrombotic factor), TIMP-1, B2M, and GDF-15.

keyFindings.title: Orthogonal Mechanisms Combine Additively
keyFindings.desc: Because omega-3 resolves lipid-mediated inflammation (resolvins/protectins), vitamin D3 modulates VDR immune/autophagy transcription, and exercise stimulates myokine and mitochondrial remodeling, their effects stacked additively on PC-PhenoAge (-2.9 to -3.8 months).

conclusions.title: Direct Randomized Proof in Older Humans (Aged 70+)
conclusions.content: DO-HEALTH provides the largest 3-year randomized factorial dataset showing that biological aging clocks remain malleable well into the eighth decade of human life, even among baseline-healthy community-dwelling older adults.

conclusions.title: Modest Annual Epigenetic Shifts Compound into Major Clinical Protection
conclusions.content: Although a 2.9 to 3.8-month slowing of PC-PhenoAge over 36 months (~8–11% slower biological aging rate) appears numerically modest, it tracked alongside a 39% reduction in pre-frailty and a 61% reduction in invasive cancer across the 2,157-person parent trial.

conclusions.title: Biomarker-Guided Personalization via Baseline Omega-3 Index
conclusions.content: The pronounced response in participants with baseline plasma EPA+DHA ≤100 ng/mL establishes that correcting subclinical omega-3 insufficiency is one of the highest-yield, lowest-risk geroprotective interventions available.

protocolImplications: Translational takeaway: The DO-HEALTH protocol uses highly accessible, clinician-verifiable daily doses—1,000 mg/day marine algae omega-3 (330 mg EPA + 660 mg DHA), 2,000 IU/day vitamin D3, and 3×30 minutes/week of progressive resistance exercise. Tracking baseline blood EPA+DHA (Omega-3 Index), 25(OH)D levels, and 2nd/3rd-generation epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, PC-PhenoAge, GrimAge2) allows objective quantification of individual biological response.
